analysis:
The only change in this PR is test-only: provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Inference/Engine/EngineV2BridgeTests.swift gains two tests at head lines ~807-839 (scopedMatchedSequence and translationCarriesStopScope). They exercise new production APIs that this batch does not include: ModelEOSPolicy.stopStringScope(modelId:), EngineV2Bridge.matchedStopSequence(candidates:generatedText:scope:), the stopStringScope parameter of EngineV2Translation.cbv2Request, and CBv2Request.stopStringScope. I only saw the base text and this test patch, so the security behavior of those APIs is unverified.

The tests assert that for a gpt-oss model a caller-supplied stop string such as '.' only counts as matched when it appears in the final channel, not in analysis text. They also assert that the scope is carried onto CBv2Request and is nil when no scope is passed. Nothing in the test file touches security-relevant behavior. It adds no secrets, network access, key handling or cache identity logic. It does not change cacheSalt handling, which the existing base test bridgeStampsCacheSalt still covers for T-041 (caller prompt_cache_key and user never become cache identity). The base-side pump-receipt and SSD hybrid checkpoint tests are unchanged.

Open question for integration, not a finding: the production change that implements stopStringScope is in other units. A reviewer of those should check three things. First, that stop-string scoping cannot let a consumer suppress or force termination in ways that alter billing usage. The max-usage billing defense and the teardown/usage framing tests exist at base. Second, that scope matching does not leak analysis-channel content (A-001) via the recorded matchedStopSequence signal. Third, that scope handling fails closed for non-GPT-OSS models. Tests alone are clean.
